title: Yakub Abdul Razak Memon v. State of Maharashtra (1993 Bombay Serial Blasts)
crime_type: Coordinated Vehicle Bombings / Terror Conspiracy / RDX Smuggling
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / TADA Special Court Greater Bombay
source: Supreme Court of India Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1359141)
ipc_sections: Section 3(2) TADA (Terrorist and Disruptive Activities Prevention Act)
location: Bombay Stock Exchange, Air India Building, Zaveri Bazaar, Mumbai, India
evidence: Recovery of unexploded RDX-laden Maruti car near Worli and scooter parked at Century Bazaar containing Tiger Memon vehicle documents
Hawala banking slips and air ticket booking records showing transit of conspirators to Islamabad via Dubai for arms training
Seizure of massive caches of RDX, detonators, and assault rifles smuggled via Shekhadi coast in Raigad district
Confessional statements recorded under Section 15 of TADA detailing secret coordination meetings at Al-Husseini building
modus_operandi: Organized crime syndicate joined forces with foreign intelligence handlers to smuggle tons of military RDX and assault weapons via coastal sea routes. Planted car bombs and suitcase explosives across 12 high-density financial and commercial landmarks in Mumbai, detonating them within a two-hour window.
personality_disorder: Calculated criminal vengeance, organizational loyalty to transnational mafia syndicates, and logistical ruthlessness.
common_traits: Coordinated multi-site vehicle-borne improvised explosive devices (VBIED)
Use of military RDX and pencil timers
Pre-coordinated family flight overseas prior to detonation
summary: First synchronized multi-target urban bomb attacks in modern history, killing 257 people. The TADA Special Court and Supreme Court convicted Yakub Memon for financing and arranging travel/logistics, leading to his execution in 2015.
